pick.name: DocuSeal
pick.why: Most generous free tier (10 requests/mo cloud, unlimited self-hosted); AGPL self-host means no lock-in; API/embedding available from one Pro seat
pick.free_limits: Cloud Basic: 10 signature-request emails/mo; self-host OSS edition unlimited (no automated reminders/SSO/webhook monitoring); Pro USD 20/user/mo; API USD 0.20/doc and requires >=1 Pro seat
pick.windows_fit: web (self-host via Docker on a Linux VM)
pick.license: AGPL-3.0 (self-host edition; licence named on GitHub)

alts.name: Zoho Sign
alts.what: Zoho e-signature with Aadhaar eSign identity
alts.why: Only mainstream tool here with Aadhaar eSign for Indian counterparties
alts.free_limits: Free: 1 user, 5 envelopes/mo; Aadhaar eSign via paid credits

alts.name: Documenso
alts.why: Polished OSS option; free cloud 5 docs/mo; Individual USD 25/mo
alts.free_limits: Free: 5 docs/mo, 10 recipients/doc; API from Individual

candidates.name: Zoho Sign
candidates.verdict: Wins when an Indian counterparty needs Aadhaar eSign

candidates.name: Documenso
candidates.verdict: Close OSS runner-up; smaller free tier

candidates.name: Leegality / Digio
candidates.verdict: Aadhaar eSign APIs, per-sign pricing (not checked)

decision: DocuSeal's free cloud tier covers a solo founder's NDAs/order forms; self-host it on a small always-free VM if volume grows. Use Zoho Sign only when an Indian client wants Aadhaar eSign.
details: Plain click/typed e-signatures are generally valid in US (ESIGN/UETA); in India the IT Act recognises electronic signatures incl. Aadhaar eSign; some documents are excluded. Verify with a lawyer.

verify.note: Confirmed: Basic gets 10 request emails/mo, Pro USD 20/user/mo, API USD 0.20/doc, AGPL-3.0, 3.3.4 on 2026-10-26. But the API needs at least one Pro seat (USD 20/mo), so 'API + embedding' isn't on the free tier. The open-source self-host edition lacks reminders, SSO and webhook monitoring.
